threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by how they still rave about the 'lovely' market at Chatsworth Road, while locals roll their eyes at the overpriced artisan bread.
Last Friday on the 35, two blokes argued over a lost phone; it turned into a karaoke showdown to 'find it'. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a hidden kiosk selling homemade baklava, I realized Neukölln is full of little treasures, just waiting to be discovered.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that doubles as a library. Grab a beer and browse through hundreds of books while waiting for your drink.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they dodge the BART delays like it’s an Olympic sport. Tourists just stand and stare at the screens.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo quietly napping on the 14, only to wake up and start singing opera when the bus hit a bump. Classic Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just for Gaudí, but the real heart beats in the small plaça bars where locals gather after work, not in the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them struggling with the metro ticket machines, pressing buttons like it's a game show and still ending up lost on the wrong line.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still go to the green grocer expecting normal prices instead of debating whether to splurge on heirloom tomatoes.
Caught a bloke sleeping with a full kebab in his hand on the 59 last night. When the bus lurched, he didn't even flinch. Proper legend.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw an old man feeding pigeons while chatting about poetry with a street artist near the canal. It felt like magic in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a Späti that doubles as an art gallery—local artists showcase their work alongside your midnight beer run.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're locals when they know not to even glance at the BART app during rush hour—it’ll just ruin your day.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: One time, a musician jumped on the 47, played a haunting tune, and by the next stop, everyone was smiling despite the rain. That’s Muni magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think a paella is the go-to dish here, but in Gràcia, it's all about the 'pintxos' and a good vermut on a Sunday afternoon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their constant fumbling with the T-10 card at the metro turnstile, like it’s a puzzle they haven’t cracked yet.
